explanation: The great sinful empire or system that stands in opposition to God, often associated with luxury, unbelief, and oppression.
Why is the holy city Jerusalem called "harlot" in this context? No, that is not correct; the term refers to a woman symbolizing a sinful empire or system that has abandoned God.
A metaphorical figure representing the great sinful empire (Babylon) and its influence over the nations of the world.
One of the seven-headed beasts in the vision, symbolizing an evil power or kingdom that has the ability to persecute God's people.
Representing seven kingdoms or forms of government; five have fallen, one exists now, and the seventh is yet to come.
One of the ten horns symbolizing ten kings or powers who will give their authority to the beast for a short time before judgment comes.
Symbolizing peoples, nations, and vast multitudes of people who are restless and chaotic.
One of the seven waters representing peoples, opinions, or kingdoms; here it is used to describe how the holy city is surrounded by streams of sin.
God's righteous decision against the evil kingdom and all who have participated in its injustice.
The pure place where God dwells, contrasted with the holy city that has been polluted by systems of sin.
